Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is: To fly, fight, and win ... Airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Global Reach and Global Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. This position is a Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel Systems (DCIPS) position implemented under Section 504, Title V of Public Law 99-569, Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 1987, as codified in Sec 1601, Chap 83 of Title 10 United States Code which sets forth Air Force policies and procedures for DCIPS. This position is in the Excepted Service. DoD Components with DCIPS positions apply Veterans' Preference to preference eligible candidates as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 USC, in accordance with the procedures provided in DoD Instruction 1400.25, Volume 2005, DCIPS Employment and Placement. If you are a veteran claiming veterans' preference, as defined by section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., you must submit documents verifying your eligibility with your application package. For additional information on DCIPS, click here
MajorDuties: DUTY 1: Develops, implements, and controls contractual, financial, and technical aspects of a project/program through designated phases of the acquisition cycle for which no closely related precedents exist. DUTY 2: Plans, organizes, directs, and coordinates activities of functional specialists including contracting, engineering, manufacturing, program control, configuration/data management, test, and logistics. DUTY 3: Reviews and directs the progress of contractors in meeting program objectives. DUTY 4: Represents the organization at executive levels within the Government and to contractor/industry representatives. DUTY 5: Prepares, presents, defends, and interprets staff studies to the Program Director and/or other management officials.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Do you enjoy challenges and seek opportunities? Are identifying problems, analyzing facts, and making recommendations some of your strong suits? Would you like to obtain the rare opportunity to participate in some of the greatest technological achievements developed? Would you like to serve your country and defend freedom in one of the most critical efforts in history? If you answered yes, then this job is for you! The Missile Defense Agency's (MDA) mission is to develop, test, and field an integrated, layered, ballistic missile defense system (BMDS) to defend the United States, its deployed forces, allies, and friends against all ranges of enemy ballistic missiles in all phases of flight. We are seeking prepared, talented, and motivated Program Analysts who seek challenges and opportunities. You will earn a competitive salary and enjoy outstanding benefits while working alongside some of the brightest, most motivated thinkers of our time.
MajorDuties: As a PROGRAM ANALYST at the NH-0343-4 some of your typical work assignments may include:?????? Serves as the Policy Interface Lead for the International and Policy Directorate (DI) responsible for assisting the Director for International and Policy in representing Missile Defense Agency (MDA) Director with the United States Government (USG) Interagency. Assists DI as the representative for Policy Coordination Committee (PCC) meetings, Missile Defense Executive Board (MDEB) Policy Committee, and as principal MDA interlocutor with OSD-Policy. Represents the Director for International and Policy in engagements with members or representatives of the USG Interagency, OSD, the Joint Staff, the military departments, Defense Agencies, and other governmental/international entities. Establishes/maintains relationships/communication channels with appropriate DoD, other U.S. government agencies, and foreign partner organizations. Analyzes/develops responses to requests for information, briefings, and guidance from OSD Policy. Supports policy planning activities to include development of strategic policy documents such as the Missile Defense Review (MDR). Serves as DI's lead for working special projects, including development of strategic messaging, support of MDA executive briefings, and review of MDA annual budget documentation. Responsible for developing multi-dimensional analyses in support of MDA's International cooperative activities. Develops recommendations based upon in-depth analysis of issues, knowledge of MDA's functional and programmatic activities, and consideration of overall missions, budgetary constraints, technological advances, political environment, and human resources. Provides advice and oversight on legislative issues/strategic communications activities as related to international affairs programs, projects, and activities. Develops/directs responses to Congressional Requests for Information, Questions for the Record, Reports to Congress, and briefing requests. Ensures timely responses to Congress, working through the Legislative Affairs staff.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Defense Threat Reduction Agency, The incumbent will be responsible for directing and managing projects within the Biological Threat Reduction Program Department (BTRP) of the Cooperative Threat Reduction Directorate (CTR). Prepares project plans, acquisition baselines, acquisition strategies, implementation plans, and funding plans for BTRP projects.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Defense Threat Reduction Agency provides cross-cutting solutions to enable the DoD, the United States Government, and international partners to DETER strategic attack against the United States and it's allies; PREVENT, reduce, and counter Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) and emerging threats; and PREVAIL against WMD-armed adversaries in crisis and conflict.
MajorDuties: As an International Program Specialist (Project Manager) at the GS-0301-11/12/13 some of your typical work assignments may include: Responsible for managing, planning, programming, budgeting and supervising the execution of multiple efforts. Directs assigned professional staff of government personnel and contractors. Responsible for identifying and assessing the assistance needs of partner countries, developing technical requirements and specifications, coordinating the efforts of other non-DOD agencies, combatant command (CCMD) assets, international partners and non-governmental organizations, and managing assigned DTRA contracts. Establishes realistic program/portfolio-wide and individual project goals, metrics and priorities; provides for the timely dissemination of program results, and keeps DTRA management, the Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD), CCMDs, and other key customers informed of progress and significant accomplishments. Directs and manages the execution of approved projects leading to biological threat reduction success, as discussed above, in accordance with federally established acquisition guidelines through the use of DTRA contracts with the U.S. and foreign firms. To accomplish this, the incumbent prepares procurement requirement specifications and documents; chairs technical source selection evaluation boards; prepares source selection recommendations; conducts detailed technical discussions with contract bidders; debriefs both winning and losing bidders on proposal deficiencies; provides frequent guidance to integrating contractors and other support organizations; monitors contractor and partner organization performance; reviews and approves all contract reports and deliverables and recommends required adjustments to existing contracts. Provides oversight for very large, complex technical contracts spanning several years duration awarded to both U.S. and foreign enterprises. Facilitates and participates in technical discussions with foreign officials concerning CTR projects. Develops close ties and a solid working relationship with project stakeholders. Represents CTR at all appropriate levels, with counterparts in the assigned geographic area, and within the U.S. inter-agency process. Provides justification to higher authority for specific technical and fiscal needs of the assigned engagements. Maintains liaison with appropriate offices and individuals to keep them abreast of significant accomplishments, program changes, and other substantive events. As the U.S. Government delegation leader on trips to foreign countries within the assigned geographic area, the incumbent oversees the performance of a diverse group of civilian, military and contractor personnel in the accomplishment of delegation objectives. As delegation lead, serves as facilitator, negotiator, and primary point of contact and principal decision-maker. Maintains liaison with U.S. Embassy personnel, foreign officials, directors of large civilian enterprises, and high-ranking and/or flag/general officers in various ministries of the governments within the assigned geographic area.

GS-12 Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes assisting with workforce planning of a federal civilian workforce; validating training and development requirements; identifying resources associated with training and development program goals and implementing program policy. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-11). GS-13 Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes developing strategies to optimize talent management programs and systems critical to the education and professional development of federal employees AND analyzing workforce structure and resources to assess the adequacy and availability of civilian training, education, and development programs specific to the civilian human resources functional community. Applicants must meet all eligibility requirements and minimum qualification requirements prescribed by OPM within 30 days of the closing date of the announcement.

This position will be recruited for at either the GS-12 or GS-13 grade level. The responsibilities listed are at the full performance level (GS-13). Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.

Responds to and coordinates with ACCMA HQs as appropriate for functional area career management activities.

Partners with DoD and DA agencies and senior leaders to forecast workforce trends and issues.

MajorDuties: Serves as the Computer Assisted Ordering Technician in a Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) location. The primary purpose of this position is to maintain accurate perpetual inventory balance on hand (BOH) levels which in turn determines optimum ordering quantities and ensures product availability for patrons. . Position responsibilities include: Maintain the Computer Assisted Ordering (CAO) system with current, accurate data to ensure optimal order quantities are calculated necessary to sustain customer demands. Use radio-frequency hand-held terminals to gather data necessary to update and adjust inventory. Record and update Balance on Hand (BOH) data; maintain perpetual inventory and audit credits. Perform daily inventory audit of items not-in-stock and overwrite items. Evaluate stock levels of all CAO categories daily by physically reviewing the storage and display shelf locations, shippers and warehouse. Interface with all levels of management and deal directly with commercial distributor/vendor stocking representatives on issues affecting CAO.

Public transportation and free parking are available.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Serve as Senior staff Director for training, plans and operations, airfield, ranges, training support center, and security on a large, multi-functional Tier 3 CONUS-based installation.
Provide strategic vision and operational management for nine Installation Services.
Manage the staff coordination for 141K maneuver training acres, 86 live fire ranges and 300 training areas to support ~115 ranges and training area events daily.

Provide guidance for general support to the Maneuver Center of Excellence (MCoE) and the Armor and Infantry Schools, and FORSCOM (1st SFAB), USASOC (two Battalions and HQs for 75th Ranger Regt), MEDCOM, and various USAR and ARNG units/activities.
Execute the planning, coordination, and execution for multiple force protection no-notice events annually; includes annual All Hazards Full Scale Exercise.
Execute the installation?s mobilization mission (Power Projection Platform, MFGI, APOE/APOD, etc.).
Manage a "tailored Emergency Operations Center" to monitor / manage crisis events and mitigate risk to the Installation.
Manage the Garrison?s personnel security programs; includes security clearance applications for processing to the DOD Consolidated Adjudication Services (CAS).

The primary purpose of this position is to function as the official point of contact (POC) for all related problems or assistance requirements for the full range of authorized beneficiaries.
Details.SubAgencyName: Defense Health Agency, Martin Army Community Hospital, Southwest Georgia
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: At the Defense Health Agency (DHA), our Mission is to support the National Defense Strategy and Service Military Departments by leading the Military Health System (MHS) as an integrated, highly reliable system of medical training, readiness, and health. As the health care delivery arm of the MHS, DHA is crucial to supporting the Department of Defense's integrated system of readiness and health. DHA manages a global health care network of military and civilian medical professionals and more than 400 military hospitals and clinics around the world. DHA is a joint, integrated Combat Support Agency that enables the Army, Navy, and Air Force medical services to provide a medically ready force and ready medical force to Combatant Commands in both peacetime and wartime. The DHA supports the delivery of integrated, affordable, and high quality health services to the MHS beneficiaries and is responsible for driving greater integration of clinical and business processes across the MHS.
MajorDuties: Serve as the Beneficiary Counseling and Assistance Coordinators (BCAC) and Debt Collection and Assistance Officers (DCAO) for local beneficiaries and Defense Health Agency (DHA) supporting regulations.

Respond to beneficiary, provider inquires on TRICARE health care delivery issues and resolves access-to-health care complaints and request for assistance. Enter data into the appropriate spreadsheet or database for record-keeping purposes.
Coordinate and presents in-service education as necessary to increase the organization staff?s awareness of the patients? perceptions and experiences to improved staff understanding and awareness.
Notify the Risk manager of cases that may have a potential litigation.

El Paso is a jewel in the desert. Nestled between the rugged Franklin Mountains and the historic Rio Grande, this dynamic border community combines the advantages of a major metropolitan center with the ambience and neighborly charm of a modern western town. Just outside Fort Bliss' gates is "Sun City", the 19th largest city and one of the safest cities for one its size in the United States. The sun shines in El Paso approximately 302 days per year, earning it the nickname "Sun City." El Paso is a thriving big city of more than 800,000, with a great history and a tremendous spirit. From nature to culture to nightlife to shopping, there is something for everyone in El Paso. A true melting pot of American and southwestern culture, the combination is noticeable everywhere.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position:This Supervisory TECH SPT DIV Chief position is located at U.S. Army Operational Test Command (OTC), Air and Missile Defense Test Directorate with duty location of Fort Bliss, Texas.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. What is the U.S. Army Test and Evaluation Command (ATEC)? ATEC is the Army's independent test and evaluation organization. We are a team of Civilian and Military personnel working together to provide America's Military with the best equipment to win and return home safely. At ATEC, we have a saying: If a Soldier rides, wears, shoots, or deploys it, we test it. ATEC is at the forefront of testing and evaluating technologies of the future from autonomous aerial/ground vehicles to hypersonic weapons. Each day, top scientists and engineers test and evaluate cutting-edge equipment. Our workforce is highly technical and skilled, comprised of more than 8,500 military, civilian, and contract personnel. Engineers, scientists, technicians, researchers, and evaluators work with innovative, advanced technologies in 24 testing and research locations across the U.S. States and around the world.
MajorDuties: Serve as Contracting Officer Representative within Operational Test Command Air and Missile Defense Test Directorate Area of Responsibility for assigned contracts.
Execute test design assignments of items integral to the instrumentation systems on systems under test by the Operational Test Command.
Serve as a subject matter expert in developing designs utilizing areas such as electronics, computer science, digital signal processing, mechanics, physical science, and/or electro-optics.

Serve as a subject matter expert in the oversight of cyber security risk management framework to support the authority to operate certification/sustainment activities on items such as instrumentation, data collection and modeling simulation systems.

Review documents such as test documents, Performance Work Statements, Task Authorization Requests, interagency support agreements, statements of work, Source Selection and Evaluation Board plan and quality surveillance plans for the organization.
Prepare the Contract Data Requirements List via the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment/sub-systems supporting the end-to-end Procure-to-Pay business process.
Provide direction for areas such as development, integration, cost, scheduling, performance, installation, verification, checkout, and testing of weapons systems under test.
Assess contractor performance to ensure compliance with quality assurance requirements.
Manage equipment maintenance for the motor pool.
Oversee vehicle accident reporting to ensure all required items of information are provided such as accident reports and Financial Liability Investigations of Property Loss.
Maintain responsibility for coordinating all maintenance requirements pertaining to Communications/Electronic.

Provide reports to individuals such as Division, Directorate, General Officers, and Technical Directors regarding areas such as test instrumentation status, readiness for test, performance, and operations resources.
Perform supervisory duties over personnel to ensure customer requirements are met.
Act as a supervisor by completing tasks such as approving and disapproving leave, resolving complaints, and counseling employees.
Assign work to subordinates based on areas such as priorities, difficulty of assignments, and the capabilities of employees.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The foundation for success of the Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) mission is our people. We have a workforce of more than 13,000, reflecting our nation's diverse cultures and backgrounds, and annual sales of more than $4 billion. We take pride in offering a valued benefit that contributes to military family readiness and enhances quality of life by providing a service that almost all military families use. As one of the few international grocery chains, we operate 236 commissaries throughout the world. We are a grocery store and a whole lot more. More information.
MajorDuties: Serves as a Computer Assisted Ordering Technician in a commissary store at a Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) facility. The primary purpose of this position is to maintain accurate perpetual inventory balance on hand (BOH) levels which in turn determines optimum ordering quantities and ensures product availability for patrons. Position responsibilities include: Maintain the Computer Assisted Ordering (CAO) system with current, accurate data to ensure optimal order quantities are calculated necessary to sustain customer demands. Use radio-frequency hand-held terminals to gather data necessary to update and adjust inventory. Record and updates Balance on Hand (BOH) data, maintains perpetual inventory and audits credits. Perform daily inventory audit of items not-in-stock and overwrite items. Evaluate stock levels of all CAO categories daily by physically reviewing the storage and display shelf locations, shippers and warehouse. Interface with all levels of management and deals directly with commercial distributor/vendor stocking representatives on issues affecting CAO.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Defense Threat Reduction Agency. The incumbent will be responsible for serving as primary Project Officer at RD-TSX location on Fort Bragg. Responsible for consolidating inputs from that location to all RD-TSX project data requirements.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Defense Threat Reduction Agency provides cross-cutting solutions to enable the DoD, the United States Government, and international partners to DETER strategic attack against the United States and it's allies; PREVENT, reduce, and counter Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) and emerging threats; and PREVAIL against WMD-armed adversaries in crisis and conflict.
MajorDuties: As a PROJECT OFFICER at the GS-0301-14 some of your typical work assignments may include: Provides RD-TSXP Program Manager with feedback on status of all project locally managed from Fort Bragg, status of personnel training and administrative requirements, and other information requirements levied by the Program Manager, Technology Branch Chief, or RD-TSX Division Chief. Serves as a Project Officer for the RD-TSXP, Program Management Branch to conduct rapid, secure, and independent assessments of critical and unique technologies and programs from approval through closeout. Ensures independence from client and other influence during assessment project planning, execution and reporting. Oversees and participates in the development of Technical Roundtables (TRT), Event Execution Documents (EED), Test Readiness Reviews (TRR) and final reports. Provides input, and approves draft final assessment reports, and then schedules and leads the review board to secure technical review input, supervise required changes to the report, and secure final approval to release the report to the client. Develops Client Requirement Documents (CRDs) to articulate client/warfighter needs, address Program Manager/Deputy Program Manager and senior leadership comments. Staffs CRDs through the approval process. As related to assessment projects, applies a wide range of qualitative and quantitative methods to routinely assess pertinent issues found during review of technical data, test concepts, assessment results, and any other information relative to the system under test or assessment. Responsible for resource management and security for RD-TSXP assessment projects. Ensures assessment project requirements, timelines, and costs don't exceed agreements contained within the Client Requirement Documents (CRD). In coordination with Program Manager/Deputy Program Manager, develops project costs and submits written requirements to the Program Manager/Deputy Program Manager and senior leadership for appropriate mix of personnel skills and resources needed for projects. Follows security directives and policies to protect classified client, RD-TSX, and other information, and Operational Security (OPSEC) sensitive RD-TSX information. Updates details of assigned project in the RD-TSX PM database or other RD-TSX data tracking applications. Serves as the Project Team leader for assigned projects. Leads teams combined of military, government civilian and contractor personnel in field environments and garrison. Ensures host nation rules and laws are followed, ensures team receives OPSEC training before OCONUS deployment. Ensures minimal attention is focused toward the RD-TSX and its mission at all times. Duties also include providing timely individual performance feedback to supporting team members' and providing the Program Manager/Deputy Program Manager written input on individual performance.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position serves as a Program Analyst for the Joint Special Operations Command. This position is located in Fort Bragg, North Carolina. Fort Bragg is a culturally diverse area with both rural and city populations, adjacent to Fayetteville and centrally located in the beautiful state of NC which enjoys a temperature year-round climate and world-renowned colleges and universities.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Review and analyze Program Objective Memorandum input for conformance with guidance and instructions.
Develop and recommend solutions to alleviate adverse impact on command resource levels in the out years and improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the command's programs.
Analyze command input, trends, and program inconsistencies considering funding and appropriation constraints and regulations
Prepare analysis of total resources (manpower and dollars) considering the command organization, missions, functions, programs, goals and objectives at the line-item level of detail.
Develop strategic plans from inception through the command's Program Objective Memorandum and budget cycles.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position serves as the Management Analyst for the Fort Bragg Garrison Resource Management Office (RMO). This position is located at Fort Bragg, North Carolina. Fort Bragg is co-located with Fayetteville, North Carolina, a culturally diverse city. Fort Bragg is known as the "Home of the Airborne and Special Operations Forces."
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. MajorDuties: Performs analytical and evaluative work to ensure that the Table of Distribution and Allowance (TDA) structure is in accordance with sound organizational concepts and that manpower resources needed are accomplished for mission success.
Conducts analysis and coordination of the Equipment portion of the TDA to validate and submit DA Form 1460-R for equipment changes.
Applies knowledge and understanding of programs such as, Manpower and Equipment Program, the Army Management Control Program to achieve program goals and objectives.
Assists in the preparation of the annual Command Plan input for Program Objective Memorandum (POM) cycles
Performs research and evaluation, conducts special studies and prepares reports/impact statements on specified Garrison matters.
Provides policy guidance and technical assistance regarding program requirements.
Prepares manpower reports for submission to higher headquarters and through channels to Garrison leadership for further analysis of manpower posture.
Coordinates personnel actions with the local Civilian Personnel Advisory Center (CPAC) and the supported directorates.
Conducts formal training sessions and briefings regarding program requirements and responsibilities.

Demonstrates knowledge of manpower related databases to include RM online, Defense Civilian Personnel Data System (DCPDS), AUTONOA, Force Management System Website (FMSWeb) and FASCLASS to analyze requirements and authorizations.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serves in the Material Integration Branch, under the Requirements Integration Division, Force Integration Directorate, G-3/5/7, and U.S. Army Forces Command (FORSCOM). as an Organizational Integrator (OI) for all Mission Command and Communications systems within FORSCOM units and as the assistant OI for Signal (SRC 11).
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Serves as a subject matter expert for the force structures of the assigned units, to include its designs and major sub-organizations, as they pertain to critical Mission Command and Communications systems and applications.
Provides technical advice and makes recommendations to the FORSCOM leadership on operational matters that affect Mission Command and Communication Systems in assigned units.
Analyzes and evaluates Army Campaign Plan (ACP) changes to remain informed of overarching decisions and policies that affect those systems.
Develops new communications techniques, establishes criteria and develops new information and approaches to solve problems.

Manages all aspects of unit availability, unit readiness (especially Battle Command as a Weapons System [BCAWS]), unit sourcing, identification of unit mission requirements, and recommended organizational changes

Ensures units comply with Army readiness guidelines throughout the ReARMM cycle by participating in the monthly ReARMM OPT, Army Synchronization Meeting, Strategic Readiness Update, and responsible for recommending who should attend meetings/VTC.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position as Program Analyst is located at USAJFK SPECIAL WARFARE CENTER & SCHOOL, Fort Bragg, North Carolina. The 2021 Federal Employee Viewpoint Survey, led by the Office of Personnel Management, showed that USASOC ranked as the #1 best place to work out of all Army subcomponents. The ranking is fully based on views from the employees who work in the organization. USASOC leads in supporting diversity, employee innovation, strategic management, and effective leadership.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. Monitors compliance with instructions by checking the accuracy validity of input.
Analyzes changes to programs and revises programming policies and procedures.

Reviews and analyzes sufficiency and accuracy of Operation and Maintenance (OM) program cost data. Analyzes USASOC Program Budget Guidance (PBG) to determine whether programmed staffing/funding levels meet requirements.

Develops, analyzes, and evaluates the USAJFKSWCS POM and program budget review, including analysis and preparation of resource requirements within imposed resource constraints to meet USASOC, USSOCOM and TRADOC objectives and missions.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Specialized experience: One year of specialized experience in 1) advising on the federal budget process from Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution System (PPBES) through Program Objective Memorandum (POM) submission; 2) ensures adequate funds are programmed to support future operations, training, readiness, sustainability, modernization, and force structure; 3) evaluate a wide variety of narrative and statistical data furnished by Program Managers in support of budget estimates, distribution of funds, tracking and reporting expenditures, reporting funds status; 4) oral communication to brief the impacts on mission accomplishments.This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service GS-11. Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this job, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone -no substitution of education for experience is permitted. You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas: Communications Problem Solving Requirements Analysis Technical Competence Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-11).

Specialized experience: one year of specialized experience which includes demonstrated experience applying analytical and evaluative techniques to the identification, consideration, and resolution of issues or problems of a procedural or factual nature, and applying conventional methods to gather, analyze, and evaluate information concerning management processes, draw conclusions, and recommend appropriate action, and skill in conducting interviews with supervisors and employees to obtain information about organizational missions, functions, and work procedures. Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is located at Evans Army Community Hospital with the Resource Management Division, Management Analysis Branch, Fort Carson, CO.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: At the Defense Health Agency (DHA), our Mission is to support the National Defense Strategy and Service Military Departments by leading the Military Health System (MHS) as an integrated, highly reliable system of medical training, readiness, and health. As the health care delivery arm of the MHS, DHA is crucial to supporting the Department of Defense's integrated system of readiness and health. DHA manages a global health care network of military and civilian medical professionals and more than 400 military hospitals and clinics around the world. DHA is a joint, integrated Combat Support Agency that enables the Army, Navy, and Air Force medical services to provide a medically ready force and ready medical force to Combatant Commands in both peacetime and wartime. The DHA supports the delivery of integrated, affordable, and high quality health services to the MHS beneficiaries and is responsible for driving greater integration of clinical and business processes across the MHS.
MajorDuties: Provide managers with objectively based information for making decisions on the administrative and programmatic aspects of agency operations and management.
Provide advisory services to improve productivity efficiency
Develop and administer survey questionnaire by adapting similar, previously used formats
Responsible for computer system operation for Medical Expense and Performance Reporting System (MEPRS).
Provide technical guidance and assistance to work centers
Collect, analyze, interpret, and correlate large amounts of statistical and narrative information about workload productivity.
Perform management studies and reviews

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is located at Evans Army Community Hospital, Resource Management, Manpower Documentation Branch.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: At the Defense Health Agency (DHA), our Mission is to support the National Defense Strategy and Service Military Departments by leading the Military Health System (MHS) as an integrated, highly reliable system of medical training, readiness, and health. As the health care delivery arm of the MHS, DHA is crucial to supporting the Department of Defense's integrated system of readiness and health. DHA manages a global health care network of military and civilian medical professionals and more than 400 military hospitals and clinics around the world. DHA is a joint, integrated Combat Support Agency that enables the Army, Navy, and Air Force medical services to provide a medically ready force and ready medical force to Combatant Commands in both peacetime and wartime. The DHA supports the delivery of integrated, affordable, and high quality health services to the MHS beneficiaries and is responsible for driving greater integration of clinical and business processes across the MHS.
MajorDuties: Assist managers and supervisors in the formulation of improvement plans and strategies.
Provide updates on strength using tools such as a Table of Distribution and Allowances (TDA).
Analyze, integrate and manage initiatives directly related to various medical programs.
Provide cost estimates for salary formulation and make a recommendations.
Recommend policy, establish methods, procedures, and processes relative to implementation.
Assist with the implementation of new manpower policies, procedures, or changes to establish policies or procedures.
Present briefings regarding assigned projects within the scope of manpower management to staff, higher headquarters, or new functional managers.
Propose solutions to management to resolve space, supplies or equipment issues.
Prepare briefings to present to management on the results of studies or surveys.
Brief the results of studies and analysis to management either verbally or using a slide show presentation.

In keeping with the Demonstration pay fixing policies, employees earning a salary that falls within this payband equivalent, may not receive an immediate pay increase (promotion) if appointed to this position. Future pay increases within the payband will be accomplished through the pay for performance management system. This position requires an active membership as a Soldier in the Army Reserve before a start date can be set. Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This is a Military Technician position with the 84th Training Command, 78th Training Division located at Fort Dix, New Jersey. This position requires an active membership as a Soldier in the Army Reserve before a start date can be set. To learn more about minimum qualifications to join the Army Reserve, visit http://www.goarmy.com/reserve/jobs.html
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This is a military technician position with the US Army Reserves. Becoming a Military Technician allows you to experience the best of two worlds by taking advantage of the opportunity to become a Citizen Soldier in the US Army Reserve Military Technician program. This enables you to receive full civil service benefits and military reserve benefits. Military Technicians are a vital link between the US Army Reserves and civil service and are one of the most important keys to combat readiness.
MajorDuties: Advise senior leadership on use of automated training systems.
Evaluate training plans and schedules to develop the Command's training program.
Conduct inspections or reviews to evaluate training operations.
Develop mobilization training plans for approval by senior leadership.
Prepare guidance on operation and training activities to ensure compliance with training quota requirements.
Prepare and submit data for budget formulation.
Recommend final decision on expenditure requests.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: The person in this position will serve as the Process Improvement Manager for a complex small market Medical Treatment Facility (MTF). The person will work independently in performing duties related to the planning, coordination, facilitation and direction of administrative processes associated with managing the facility's Lean Six Sigma (LSS) / Process Improvement Program, training and initiatives.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: At the Defense Health Agency (DHA), our Mission is to support the National Defense Strategy and Service Military Departments by leading the Military Health System (MHS) as an integrated, highly reliable system of medical training, readiness, and health. As the health care delivery arm of the MHS, DHA is crucial to supporting the Department of Defense's integrated system of readiness and health. DHA manages a global health care network of military and civilian medical professionals and more than 400 military hospitals and clinics around the world. DHA is a joint, integrated Combat Support Agency that enables the Army, Navy, and Air Force medical services to provide a medically ready force and ready medical force to Combatant Commands in both peacetime and wartime. The DHA supports the delivery of integrated, affordable, and high quality health services to the MHS beneficiaries and is responsible for driving greater integration of clinical and business processes across the MHS.
MajorDuties: Serve as the change agent in administering, facilitating, and/or performing the steps necessary to create initiative action plans and business cases.
Serve as the Medical Treatment Facility's (MTF) Certified Six Sigma Black Belt.
Develop and/or evaluate long-range project proposals to determine their suitability as Continuous Process Improvement (CPI) projects.
Develop policies and procedures to ensure integration of performance improvement functions in accordance with standards and requirements.
Direct the annual appraisal of the facility-wide Performance Improvement Program.
Serve as a Trainer/Mentor of Lean Six Sigma and process improvements for the Medical Treatment Facility (MTF).
Provide project status reports to internal and external customers as well as all levels of the Medical Treatment Facility (MTF) management.
Details.Education: FOREIGN EDUCATION: If you are using education completed in foreign colleges or universities to meet the qualification requirements, you must show the education credentials have been evaluated by a private organization that specializes in interpretation of foreign education programs and such education has been deemed equivalent to that gained in an accredited U.S. education program; or full credit has been given for the courses at a U.S. accredited college or university. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. Current Department of Army Civilian Employees Current Department of Defense (DOD) Civilian Employee (non-Army) Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel System (DCIPS) Interchange Agreement Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Land Management Workforce Flexibility Act Non-Department of Defense (DoD) Transfer Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Spouse Preference (MSP) Eligible Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA) of 1998 In order to qualify, you must meet the experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: 1) conducting analysis to develop courses of action for senior leadership; 2) planning, programming, budgeting, and allocating resources across the command; 3) developing products such as information papers, presentations and correspondence for senior leaders; AND 4) planning and programming analysis including methods and procedures for evaluating and projecting out-year resource posture at command unit level. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed ­at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-13). Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this job, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone--no substitution of education for experience is permitted. You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas: Leadership Oral Communication Planning and Evaluating Program Management Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-13).

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This is a Supervisory Program Analyst position located with TRADOC G-8 at Fort Eustis, VA. Fort Eustis, VA is located in Newport News, between historic Williamsburg and Virginia Beach. Transportation includes convenient interstate and major highways connecting the city to neighboring Hampton, York County, Gloucester, Norfolk, Portsmouth, Suffolk, and Smithfield. The Tidewater area has all the conveniences of a big city with the charm of small town and rural areas.
Details.SubAgencyName: TRADOC Deputy Chief of Staff, G-8
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Serves as Supervisory Program Analyst working in the Planning, Analysis and Evaluation Directorate (PAED), Deputy Chief of Staff for Resource Management, G-8 (DCS, G-8).

Identifies and defines issues, develops alternative courses of action, and presents findings and recommendations to Senior TRADOC leadership for planning, programming, budgeting, and allocating resources across the command.
Serves as staff authority on interpretations of planning and programming regulations and policy guidance issued.
Responsible for managing and conducting Army Command (ACOM) strategic resource planning, managing, and controlling program analysis for all TRADOC programs.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This is a Mobilization Support Plans/Operations Officer position located at Fort Eustis, Virginia. Fort Eustis is located in Newport News, between historic Williamsburg and Virginia Beach. Transportation includes convenient interstate and major highways connecting the city to neighboring Hampton, York County, Gloucester, Norfolk, Portsmouth, Suffolk, and Smithfield. The Tidewater area has all the conveniences of a big city with the charm of small town and rural areas.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Serves as the installation Mobilization Support Plans/Operations Officer, assist in all matters pertaining to Mobilization, Plans and Operations for the US Army Support Activity, Fort Eustis (ASA).
Plans, coordinates, prepares, and executes current mobilization and de-mobilization operations and support.
Develops concepts, strategies, and contingency plans in support of Active Duty \ Reserve Component units and individuals for mobilization and de-mobilization.
Coordinates changes in the Individual Manning allocation to the MOBTDA with command organizational elements, Resource Management, and Force Management.
Serves as the primary command advisor and subject matter expert on contingency operations planning and exercise execution.
Develops plans for all exercises and operations.
Prepares and presents briefings and reports for the installation commander and senior staff as well as visiting general officers and high level SES officials.
Oversees the Plans and Operations on matters and policies relating to personnel management.
Plans, assigns, and evaluates work of subordinates.
Supervises permanent, term, and/or temporary Federal civilian and military employees.

Details.JobSummary: This announcement gathers applications from those seeking consideration to fill a Store Associate position in one or more of the listed commissary store locations. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The foundation for success of the Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) mission is our people. We have a workforce of more than 13,000, reflecting our nation's diverse cultures and backgrounds, and annual sales of more than $4 billion. We take pride in offering a valued benefit that contributes to military family readiness and enhances quality of life by providing a service that almost all military families use. As one of the few international grocery chains, we operate 236 commissaries throughout the world. We are a grocery store and a whole lot more. Commissary Website
MajorDuties: Serves as a Store Associate working either independently or as part of a team in any assigned retail area of a commissary store within the Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) system. Work involves performing the full range of standard Store Associate assignments and resolving recurring problems. Typical assignments depend on the individual store and store management requirements. Position responsibilities include: Assisting customers by answering questions such as item price or location, and handling bulky/heavy items. Operating an electronic checkout system to record unit price, total customer purchase, and make change. Performing a variety of duties in handling, preparing and maintaining stock levels of grocery and produce items. Reviewing stock levels and gathering inventory data in order to maintain the Computer Assisted Ordering (CAO) system. Preparing and maintaining a variety of documents to order commissary items, reconcile invoices and submit requisitions. Maintaining security, safety, and sanitation practices and procedures. Qualified - Candidates who meet the minimum qualifications and are proficient in some but not all of the position's requirements. Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This is a Training Systems Management Specialist position located at the Army Training Support Center, Fort Eustis, VA. Fort Eustis, VA is located in Newport News, between historic Williamsburg and Virginia Beach. Surrounding areas include Hampton, Norfolk, Portsmouth, Chesapeake and Virginia Beach. The Hampton Roads/Tidewater area has all the conveniences of a big city with charm of small town and rural areas.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. MajorDuties: Document and crosswalk research needs to existing capability gaps, Program of Record (POR) requirements and training/modernization strategies.
Coordinate with CAC-T TPOs, COE CDIDs/DOTs and Army University for their future Training and Education technology needs through personal contacts, site visits, meetings, and document staffing.

Supports the day-to-day management/execution of Training Management Division operations.

Conduct required and assigned technology needs analysis of documented Training and Education (T and E) gaps and needs, correlated with future training and operational modernization strategies to accurately assess future research and technology needs.
Serves as the G-3/5/7 Internal Control Administrator for the Army Internal Management Control Program (ICMP).

Serves as a subject matter expert, technical authority and advisor to Director, Training Support Analysis, and Integration ? Army Training Support Center (ATSC), Combined Arms Center-Training (CAC-T) and other TRADOC staff elements.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This is a military technician position with 80th Training Command, (TASS) 5 Brigade (BN), 102 Division (DIV) located in Fort Gordon, GA. This position requires an active membership as a Soldier in the Army Reserve before a start date can be set. To learn more about minimum qualifications to join the Army Reserve, visit http://www.goarmy.com/reserve/jobs.html
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This is a military technician position with the US Army Reserves. Becoming a Military Technician allows you to experience the best of two worlds by taking advantage of the opportunity to become a Citizen Soldier in the US Army Reserve Military Technician program. This enables you to receive full civil service benefits and military reserve benefits. Military Technicians are a vital link between the US Army Reserves and civil service and are one of the most important keys to combat readiness.
MajorDuties: Serve as a Staff Operations and Training Specialist in an Army Reserve Brigade or equivalent sized unit.
Provide technical guidance to subordinate elements, higher headquarters, and general staff members on mobilization training plans.
Conduct training for the command and subordinate unit personnel on the use of Army Training Requirements Reporting System (ATRRS).
Formulate guidance and participate in conducting mobilization workshops for subordinate units in support of their mobilization mission.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Your resume and supporting documents must show that you meet the qualifications (below) for the grade level or levels for which you are applying. When using education to qualify, the education must have equipped you with the knowledge and ability to perform the work of the position, as evidenced by on-the-job-training in food retail management or an internship or practicum in food retail management. Qualifications and requirements must be met by the closing date. For GS-11: (A) one year of specialized experience equivalent to at lest the GS-9 grade level or equivalent to at least GS-9 under other Federal service pay systems, private sector, or military, OR (B) three full years of progressively higher graduate level education leading to such a degree, or LL.M. (if related) with major study in business administration, public administration, agricultural economics (food industry management), or other fields related to the position, OR (C) a combination of experience and education that equals 100% of the qualification requirements. Specialized experience is demonstrated knowledge of retail procurement and distribution methods; principles, procedures, and techniques of retail food merchandising and retail food store management; and developments in commercial retail food store items, equipment, and practices. Examples of creditable qualifying specialized experience include: (1) Managing a commissary store, supermarket, or similar type of commercial retail food store; (2) Managing a department in a retail food store; (3) Planning, standardizing, or controlling operations in an assigned group of retail food stores; (4) Developing, interpreting, or applying policies, procedures, and operating standards for use in a retail food store; and (5) Providing technical advice on merchandising and operational matters pertaining to grocery, meats, and produce supplies, as well as front-end operations. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service program (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. See the Group Coverage Qualification Standard for Administrative and Management Positions and Individual Occupational Requirement for the Commissary Management Series for more information about qualifications and/or combining experience and education to meet the minimum qualifications. By the announcement closing date you must also meet the following requirements: -Time-in-grade applies to the promotion of current and former federal employees who hold or have held a permanent GS position in either the competitive or excepted service in the previous 52 weeks. Generally, you must serve at least 52 weeks at the next lower grade level to be considered for promotion. See the Required Documents section for information about the documents to include in your application package to show you meet time-in-grade. Current federal employees applying under VEOA eligibility are subject to time-in-grade. -Time after competitive appointment. Current federal civilian employees must have completed at least 90 days of federal civilian service since their latest non-temporary appointment from a competitive referral certificate. For this requirement, a competitive appointment is one where you applied to and were appointed from an announcement open to "All US Citizens."

Details.JobSummary: Serves as Store Manager of a Commissary having the full range of departments. Incumbent exercises full responsibility to plan, direct, coordinate and control the diverse day-to-day retail operations of the Sales Store. On a recurring basis may be required to perform department manager duties.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The foundation for success of the Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) mission is our people. We have a workforce of more than 13,000, reflecting our nation's diverse cultures and backgrounds, and annual sales of more than $4 billion. We take pride in offering a valued benefit that contributes to military family readiness and enhances quality of life by providing a service that almost all military families use. As one of the few international grocery chains, we operate 236 commissaries throughout the world. We are a grocery store and a whole lot more. More information.
MajorDuties: Position responsibilities include: Planning, directing, coordinating and controlling the diverse day-to-day commissary department operation. Resolving employee and customer complaints. Acting as department manager (produce/meat/grocery). Supervising department managers engaged in the operation of the store. Providing guidance and training to subordinates in the execution of the display program. Conducting periodic inspections for compliance with sanitation and safety requirements. Assuring item requisitions are made to maintain appropriate stock levels. Providing guidance and training to subordinates in the execution of the inventory requirements. Ensuring that all inventories are conducted timely and accurately as required. In accordance with the current CCP Manual, applicants are responsible for the completeness and accuracy of their application/resume and must follow the instructions in the vacancy announcement in order to receive consideration. We encourage you to read the entire announcement before starting the application process. By 11:59 ET on the announcement closing date, you must meet qualifications, conditions of employment, and other stated requirements, and submit a complete resume and all applicable required documents and select at least one eligibility that applies to you. When choosing your eligibility or eligibilities, carefully read the explanation as it will identify additional documents you must submit with your application package to prove you meet that eligibility. All submitted documents must be legible. Illegible documents may result in you being marked ineligible. Additionally, failure to meet qualifications and/or requirements, submit a complete resume, submit required documents, or select an eligibility applicable to you will result in you being ineligible for this position. Applicants who disqualify themselves receive no further consideration.
Details.Education: Education used to qualify for this position must be from an accredited school or educational institution recognized by the U.S. Department of Education and a copy of your transcript is required as part of your application package. For the application process, unofficial transcripts are acceptable if they contain the applicant's name, the name of the school, the date and degree that was awarded, and the list of classes and credits earned. Failure to provide transcripts will result in you being rated ineligible for this position. If selected, you must provide an official transcript before we set your entrance on duty date. Foreign Education. All current DeCA employees, regardless of location or human resources service provider, must submit a copy of a recent SF50 showing your current position title, pay plan-series-grade, tenure and position occupied. If you are applying for a higher grade than you currently hold you must also submit SF 50s to verify you held the next lower grade level for at least 52 weeks (called the time-in-grade requirement). All current Department of Defense (DoD) employees can access MyBiz and/or eOPF to obtain copies of their SF 50s. Claiming Veterans' Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA) eligibility? Your application package must include a copy of your DD214, Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty, showing the character of service. The Member 4 copy provides this information and is preferred. Additionally, if you are claiming VEOA eligibility under the following circumstances: Future military retirees must include a copy of their terminal leave request, if applicable, AND (1) a copy of their retirement DD214 [Member 4 copy] OR (2) a certification document* OR (3) a copy of their retirement letter. Future military separatees must include a copy of their terminal leave request, if applicable, AND (1) a copy of their most recent DD214 [Member 4 copy] OR (2) a certification document* OR (3) a copy of their most recent active duty orders. If you are currently serving on active duty and expected to be released or discharged within the next 120 days: A written document from the armed forces certifying the service member is expected to be discharged or released from active duty service in the armed forces under honorable conditions not later than 120 days after the date the certificate is signed is required. The certification must be on letterhead signed by the adjutant, personnel officer, unit commander or higher headquarters and include your rank, dates of active duty service, type of discharge, character of service, and, if applicable, the date your terminal leave begins. This document is sometimes called a Statement of Service. If selected, additional documentation may be required prior to appointment Notes for those claiming VEOA eligibility:1. Failing to submit all required documents may affect adjudication of your VEOA eligibility claim.2. Active duty military members who are selected may not be appointed to a position unless on terminal leave or already separated.3. You are required to provide your final DD214 upon issuance, if it was not part of your application package.4. Within the DoD, appointment of retired military members to a civilian position within 180 days immediately after retirement is subject to the provisions of 5 U.S.C. 3326.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This Management Analyst is located at the Operational Test Command (OTC), G6, Customer Support Division with duty location of Fort Hood, Texas.
Details.SubAgencyName: Operational Test Command (OTC), G6, Customer Support Division
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. The U.S. Army Operational Test Command (OTC), in collaboration with our Test and Evaluation partners, conducts independent operational testing to inform acquisition and fielding decisions for Army and select multi-service Warfighting systems. Fort Hood is located near Killeen, Texas halfway between Austin and Waco, about 60 miles from each, within the U.S. state of Texas. For more information, please visit the Fort Hood site at https://home.army.mil/hood/index.php
MajorDuties: Process all Privacy Act and Freedom of Information Act requests and reports the requests as required. Serve as the Contract Officer Representative (COR) for numerous wireless contracts and the command's copier contract in support of test teams and OTC operations. Responsible for the planning and execution of the command's printing and publication program. Serve as the single Records Management Officer for entire command, advising the command on all matters related to records management, specifically the Army Records Information Management System (ARIMS) and performs inspections. Serve as the directorate representative for the Management Information Control Program. Serve as a procurement specialist to the Customer Support Division and to the G6 Directorate. Serve as the Official Mail Room Manager ensuring proper operation of the facility. Serve as the subject matter expert (SME), advising installation and senior leadership on organizational supply management.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The foundation for success of the Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) mission is our people. We have a workforce of more than 13,000, reflecting our nation's diverse cultures and backgrounds, and annual sales of more than $4 billion. We take pride in offering a valued benefit that contributes to military family readiness and enhances quality of life by providing a service that almost all military families use. Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is located with the Communications Security (COMSEC) Compliance Division at Fort Huachuca, Arizona.
Details.SubAgencyName: Integrated Logistics Support Center (ILSC), Communications Security Logistics Activity (CSLA)
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. Fort Huachuca is located 75 miles southeast of Tucson, AZ. Fort Huachuca, Cochise County's largest employer, is a busting hub for three of the fastest-growing missions in Department of Defense: Military Intelligence, Cyber-Security and Unmanned Aircraft Systems. Fort Huachuca enjoys sunny days and starry nights with an average daytime temperature of 74 degrees, making it an ideal location for diverse recreational activities. For more information on relocation to Fort Huachuca/Sierra Vista area, please visit Fort Huachuca website at https://home.army.mil/huachuca/ or the Sierra Vista Chamber of Commerce at https://www.sierravistaareachamber.com. The mission of the Communications Security Logistics Activity (CSLA) is to serve as the Army Commodity Manager for all Communications Security (COMSEC) materiel.
MajorDuties: Plans and integrates CSLA's business and marketing efforts and serves as the C2 CSLA coordinator and key staff advisor.
Helps to develop marketing and business strategies and events aimed at highlighting CSLA's effectiveness.
Help to create an accurate understanding and perception of CSLA as the pre-eminent provider of products and services throughout the defense community.
Responsibility for Global INFOSEC Partnership Conference, Static Display Design and Development, Design and Development of Promotional Tools.

Responsible Directors conferences, National Joint Military-Industry Symposia, Home on Home Conferences, Advance Planning Briefings to Industry, VIP Visitor Program, AMC Command Reviews, and Command Overview Briefings.

Plans and executes events and secures the support and cooperation of functional specialists whose support audio visual television production, display designers, graphic artists, writer-editors and Transportation.
Directs and oversees the preparation and staffing of program proposals.
Convenes meetings and conferences for the purpose of providing advice and consultation within subject matter areas to resolve matters of policy interpretation

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Your resume and supporting documents must show that you meet the qualifications (below) for the grade level or levels for which you are applying. When using education to qualify, the education must have equipped you with the knowledge and ability to perform the work of the position, as evidenced by on-the-job-training in food retail management or an internship or practicum in food retail management. For GS-11: (A) one year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-9 grade level or equivalent to at least GS-9 under other Federal service pay systems, private sector, or military, OR (B) Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or three full years of progressively higher graduate level education leading to such a degree, or LL.M. (if related) with major study in business administration, public administration, agricultural economics (food industry management), or other fields related to the position, OR (C) a combination of experience and education that equals 100% of the qualification requirements. Specialized experience is demonstrated knowledge of retail procurement and distribution methods; principles, procedures, and techniques of retail food merchandising and retail food store management; and developments in commercial retail food store items, equipment, and practices. Examples of creditable qualifying specialized experience include: (1) Managing a commissary store, supermarket, or similar type of commercial retail food store; (2) Managing a department in a retail food store; (3) Planning, standardizing, or controlling operations in an assigned group of retail food stores; (4) Developing, interpreting, or applying policies, procedures, and operating standards for use in a retail food store; and (5) Providing technical advice on merchandising and operational matters pertaining to grocery, meats, and produce supplies, as well as front-end operations. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service program (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. See the Group Coverage Qualification Standard for Administrative and Management Positions and Individual Occupational Requirement for the Commissary Management Series for more information about qualifications and/or combining experience and education to meet the minimum qualifications. By the announcement closing date you must also meet the following requirements: Time-in-grade applies to the promotion of current and former federal employees who hold or have held a permanent GS position in either the competitive or excepted service in the previous 52 weeks. Generally, you must serve at least 52 weeks at the next lower grade level to be considered for promotion. See the Required Documents section for information about the documents to include in your application package to show you meet time-in-grade. Time after competitive appointment. Current federal civilian employees must have completed at least 90 days of federal civilian service since their latest non-temporary appointment from a competitive referral certificate. For this requirement, a competitive appointment is one where you applied to and were appointed from an announcement open to "All US Citizens."

Details.JobSummary: Serves as the Store Administrator and Assistant Store Director, fully participating in the management of all store activities. Provides management advice and guidance to other store division managers, as necessary. Assists managers in the development of major programs and departmental goals and objectives, setting specific priorities and schedules to complete work.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The foundation for success of the Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) mission is our people. We have a workforce of more than 13,000, reflecting our nation's diverse cultures and backgrounds, and annual sales of more than $4 billion. We take pride in offering a valued benefit that contributes to military family readiness and enhances quality of life by providing a service that almost all military families use. As one of the few international grocery chains, we operate 236 commissaries throughout the world. We are a grocery store and a whole lot more. More information.
MajorDuties: Through subordinate supervisors is directly responsible for all activities of the Front End Department, Customer Service Department, and Store Operations Department. Manages all functions associated with store accounting and budgeting, ordering and receiving, personnel liaison actions, development of performance plans, public affairs programs, EEO, coordination/liaison with the host command; and other business administration aspects of the commissary. Promotes the goals and objectives of EEO and Affirmative Action Programs. Position responsibilities include: Serving as the Assistant Commissary Officer, responsible for all store administration functions, and fully sharing in the overall management, direction and control of the commissary. Analyzing a variety of management reports to determine efficiency of operations and to recommend or implement changes. Developing budget estimates and monitoring program obligations and expense targets. Acting as store sanitation coordinator; establishing controls for prevention of pilferage and ensuring that sanitation, safety and security precautions are observed. Being responsible for all personnel functions within the commissary, such as staffing, recruitment and the development of performance standards. Promoting DeCA goals and objectives of the EEO and Affirmative Action Program. Representing the commissary at a variety of commander's meetings, such as the Commissary Advisory Council and Base Civil Engineering meetings. Monitoring surveys, customer service training, and customer's suggestions and ideas.
