MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. Current Department of Army Civilian Employees Current Department of Defense (DOD) Civilian Employee (non-Army) Executive Order (E.O.) 12721 Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Land Management Workforce Flexibility Act Military Spouses, under Executive Order (E.O.) 13473 Non-Appropriated Fund Instrumentality (NAFI) Non-Department of Defense (DoD) Transfer Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Interchange Agreement Eligible Postal Service/Peace Corps and Other Unique Authorities Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Spouse Preference (MSP) Eligible Reinstatement Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA) of 1998 In order to qualify, you must meet the education AND experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Basic Requirement for Economist: A. Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in economics that includes 21 semester hours in economics and 3 semester hours in statistics, accounting, or calculus. OR B. Combination of Education and Experience: Courses equivalent to a major in economics, as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes conducting economic analysis of benefits, costs, feasibility, and impacts of water resources projects; using econometrics, statistics, and computer modeling to conduct economic analysis; preparing reports and other documentation of economic analysis methodology and results. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-11). Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this job, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone--no substitution of education for experience is permitted. You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas: Computer Literacy Customer Service (Clerical/Technical) Economics and Accounting Financial Management Analysis Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-11).

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Looking for a great place to work? The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) is one of the best! In 2020, USACE ranked #2 of government large-agency subcomponent! USACE is one of the world's premier public engineering, design, and construction management agencies. We serve the American people, striving to provide the most effective engineering and environmental science solutions to the nation's complex problems affecting national security, the economy and the environment in which we live. USACE offers a team-inspiring and collaborative work environment; providing challenging and rewarding careers across a variety of disciplines. We rely on leaders with vision, creativity, and programmatic and technical expertise to lead us into the future. Align your talents with your passion and find out why the U. S. Army Corps of Engineers is a great place to work! The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. To learn more about the Sacramento District, please visit: http://www.spk.usace.army.mil/
MajorDuties: Serves as a senior analyst in the South Pacific Division Continuing Authorities Production Center, leading and completing major economic evaluation studies and assessments, as well as other types of socio-economic analyses.
Responsible for several studies or portions of studies being conducted simultaneously.
Conducts analyses of the economic cost, benefits, feasibility, and impacts of proposed water resource projects.

Uses applied research techniques such as econometrics, statistical and mathematical computations, computer modeling, and application of traditional and newly-published theories and empirical findings from economics and other disciplines.
Prepares written memoranda, study documentation, and formal reports to present and describe the components of each analysis and study conducted.

Participate with trial attorneys to develop strategy for and defense against claims to be heard before the Armed Forces Board of Contract Appeals.

All applicants tentatively selected for DLA employment in a testing designated position are subject to urinalysis to screen for illegal drug use prior to appointment. Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serves as a Postmaster and Postal Operations Officer with technical and administrative oversight for the efficiency and effectiveness of the total postal operations in a US Army overseas Military Postal Service.
Details.SubAgencyName: USAG Directorate of Human Resources- Postal Branch
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This position is located in Kaiserslautern, Germany OR Baumholder, Germany. For additional information please visit https://home.army.mil/rheinland-pfalz/.
MajorDuties: Serve as a Postmaster and Postal Operations Officer with technical and administrative oversight for the efficiency and effectiveness of the total postal operations in a US Army overseas Military Postal Service area of responsibility.
Perform postal audits designed to ensure the most effective and efficient operation.
Periodically reviews and discusses adequacy of policies, principles, and procedures.
Postmaster show initiative and judgment in determining whether pertinent regulations are being properly interpreted and applied.
Conduct quarterly inspections of unit owned mailrooms to reflect changes applicable/command directives.
Prepares reports for higher echelons ensuring data is correct and reporting requirements are met on schedule.
Conducts Postal training for staff personnel.
Makes changes to the organization, reassigns employees, adjusts work distribution and assignment of functions.
Attend quarterly meetings with commercial service providers.

Details.JobSummary: This announcement gathers applications from those seeking consideration to fill a Store Associate position in one or more of the listed commissary store locations. As vacancies occur in the 90-day period after this announcement closes, and in accordance with category rating procedures, applicants evaluated as qualified and appointable, and who submit all required documents are referred to hiring managers for selection consideration. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The foundation for success of the Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) mission is our people. We have a workforce of more than 13,000, reflecting our nation's diverse cultures and backgrounds, and annual sales of more than $4 billion. We take pride in offering a valued benefit that contributes to military family readiness and enhances quality of life by providing a service that almost all military families use. As one of the few international grocery chains, we operate 236 commissaries throughout the world. We are a grocery store and a whole lot more. More information.
MajorDuties: Serves as a Store Associate working either independently or as part of a team in any assigned retail area of a commissary store within the Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) system. Work involves performing the full range of standard Store Associate assignments and resolving recurring problems. Typical assignments depend on the individual store and store management requirements. Position responsibilities include: Assisting customers by answering questions such as item price or location, and handling bulky/heavy items. Operating an electronic checkout system to record unit price, total customer purchase, and make change. Performing a variety of duties in handling, preparing and maintaining stock levels of grocery and produce items. Reviewing stock levels and gathering inventory data in order to maintain the Computer Assisted Ordering (CAO) system. Preparing and maintaining a variety of documents to order commissary items, reconcile invoices and submit requisitions. Maintaining security, safety, and sanitation practices and procedures. The General Schedule (GS) Base Salary Table was used to identify the salary range appearing at the beginning of this announcement. Actual salaries depend on the location selected. Refer to Salary Tables to locate salaries for a specific location. You are responsible for the completeness and accuracy of your application package. All submitted documents must be legible. Failure to meet qualifications, requirements and/or conditions of employment or to submit a complete resume and required documents may result in you being ineligible for this position. Ineligible applicants receive no further consideration. We encourage you to read the entire announcement before starting the application process and to follow all instructions.

Highly Qualified - Candidates who possess the type and quality of experience that exceeds the position's minimum qualifications. Qualified - Candidates who meet the minimum qualifications and are proficient in some but not all of the position's requirements. If your claim for 10-point preference is based on a service-connected disability of 10% or more as determined by the Department of Veterans Affairs (DVA), you must include a copy of your VA letter (dated 1991 or later) certifying the service-connected disability of 10% or more. Future military retirees must include a copy of their terminal leave request, if applicable, AND (1) a copy of their retirement DD214 [Member 4 copy] OR (2) a certification document* OR (3) a copy of their retirement letter. Future military separatees must include a copy of their terminal leave request, if applicable, AND (1) a copy of their most recent DD214 [Member 4 copy] OR (2) a certification document* OR (3) a copy of their most recent active duty orders. *A written document from the armed forces certifying the service member is expected to be discharged or released from active duty service in the armed forces under honorable conditions not later than 120 days after the date the certificate is signed. The certification must be on letterhead signed by the adjutant, personnel officer, unit commander or higher headquarters and include your rank, dates of active duty service, type of discharge, character of service, and, if applicable, the date your terminal leave begins. This document is sometimes called a Statement of Service. Notes for those claiming veterans' preference: 1. Active duty military members who are selected may not be appointed to a position unless on terminal leave or already separated. 2. You are required to provide your final DD214 upon issuance, if it was not part of your application package. 3. Within the DoD, appointment of retired military members to a civilian position within 180 days immediately after retirement is subject to the provisions of 5 U.S.C. 3326. Claiming Military Spouse Preference. You must be the spouse of an active duty member of the armed forces, and your application package must include the Military Spouse PPP Self-Certification Checklist AND proof of marriage to the military service member (e.g., marriage certificate, marriage license), AND a copy of the military member's PCS orders. Your application package must include a copy of your agency-specific ICTAP eligibility notice or a copy of your separation personnel action form AND a copy of your most recent performance appraisal AND a copy of your most recent SF 50 or agency notification of personnel action showing your current position, grade level, and duty location. Separation personnel actions do not include a certificate/notice of expected separation.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Serves as program analyst responsible for direction and operation of the Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution System (PPBES) activity within ACCMA and responsible for program analysis and evaluation (PAE).

Develops courses of action to address resource issues to Army leadership through the Program Evaluation Groups (PEG) Executive Board and the Program and Budget Committee.

Responsible for researching and developing objective-based positions for ACCMA and senior Army Leadership decision-making on training, education, and professional development and leadership programs and issues.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: The mission of the DHA is to serve as a Combat Support Agency and lead the MHS integration of readiness and health to deliver the Quadruple Aim: improved readiness, better health, better care, and lower cost. This position supports the mission of the Defense Health Agency (DHA), TRICARE (J10) Health Plan, Healthcare Optimization, Access to Care Division and it is located in Falls Church, VA.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: At the Defense Health Agency (DHA), our Mission is to support the National Defense Strategy and Service Military Departments by leading the Military Health System (MHS) as an integrated, highly reliable system of medical training, readiness, and health. As the health care delivery arm of the MHS, DHA is crucial to supporting the Department of Defense's integrated system of readiness and health. DHA manages a global health care network of military and civilian medical professionals and more than 400 military hospitals and clinics around the world. DHA is a joint, integrated Combat Support Agency that enables the Army, Navy, and Air Force medical services to provide a medically ready force and ready medical force to Combatant Commands in both peacetime and wartime. The DHA supports the delivery of integrated, affordable, and high quality health services to the MHS beneficiaries and is responsible for driving greater integration of clinical and business processes across the MHS.
MajorDuties: Serves as a referral management subject matter expert with extensive expanding knowledge of legislation, administrative law, Federal regulations, Service regulations, DoD Directives/Instructions (DoDD/DoDIs), and Public Laws (PLs), etc.
Continually guide the IRMAC and RMCs and their MTFs in effectively and efficiently performing referral management and access to care activities within the MTF.
Formulates short and long-range direct care capacity, access to care and managed care planning guidance in accordance with broad agency program policies and objectives to meet program goals.

Coordinates with fellow action officers, a variety of stakeholders and MTFs to ensure corporate and enterprise level policy development is consistent with supporting a responsive system of choice to provide quality health services.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Benefits of joining U.S. Army Garrison Yuma, Yuma, AZ, include ride share opportunities; on-post surplus housing; and access to Morale, Welfare & Recreation services like child-care and youth activities for school-aged children, food and beverage facilities, fitness center, pool, and discount military theme park tickets. For those living on-post there is an on-post elementary school for grades kindergarten thru 5th grade. Benefits of being an Army Professional include unique training and professional development opportunities, DoD and Federal Leadership Development programs, paid federal holidays, sick leave and annual leave accrued per pay period based on time in service, retirement benefits, 401K matching contributions, work life enrichments such Employee Assistance Programs, and the Army Civilian Fitness and Health Promotion Program. YPG is located near the Arizona-California-Mexico border, approximately 15 miles north of the outskirts of the city of Yuma (pop 87,000), Arizona. Yuma is a 2.5-hour drive from San Diego, CA and Phoenix, AZ, along Interstate Highway 8, and a 5-6 hour drive from Las Vegas, NV, in the heart of the great Sonoran desert where the US Army tests medium and long range artillery, aircraft target acquisition equipment and armament, armored and wheeled vehicles, and a variety of munitions, and personnel and supply parachute systems to ensure that America's ground forces have the equipment necessary to win our nation's battles.

Details.JobSummary: The position(s) covered by this vacancy announcement is in the Department of Defense (DoD) Acquisition Workforce Personnel Demonstration Project (AcqDemo). For more information please see: AcqDemo This position is part of the Missile Defense Agency.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Do you enjoy challenges and seek opportunities? Are identifying problems, analyzing facts, and making recommendations some of your strong suits? Would you like to obtain the rare opportunity to participate in some of the greatest technological achievements developed? Would you like to serve your country and defend freedom in one of the most critical efforts in history? If you answered yes, then this job is for you! The Missile Defense Agency's (MDA) mission is to develop, test, and field an integrated, layered, ballistic missile defense system (MDS) to defend the United States, its deployed forces, allies, and friends against all ranges of enemy ballistic missiles in all phases of flight. We are seeking prepared, talented, and motivated E-Business Development Specialists who seek challenges and opportunities. You will earn a competitive salary and enjoy outstanding benefits while working alongside some of the brightest, most motivated thinkers of our time.
MajorDuties: This position is being filled under the memorandum from the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness (USD(P&R)) "Expansion of Direct Hire Authority for Certain Personnel of the Department of Defense," dated October 15, 2021. As a E-Business Development Specialist at the NH-1101-4 some of your typical work assignments may include: Serve as MDA's E-Business primary representative to DoD's Defense Pricing & Contracting E-Business Directorate and integrated working groups and to the Defense Logistics Agency's Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) and Enterprise Contract Writing System (ECWM) Program Management Office and 4th Estates working groups. Lead E-Business Team as MDA's Government Functional and Technical primary point of contact regarding MDA's resource requirements, system(s) usage, access and management of E-Business tools service releases, outages, updates and applicable servers. Provide expert direction, assistance, support, and oversight in the development of implementation strategies, policies, procedure, and functional requirements for E-Business tools, metrics and reporting, and data analytics related to DoD's Electronic Business (E-Business) initiatives. Responsible for overall management of MDA's E-Business Service Helpdesk and Dashboard for Federal, DoD and MDA Acquisition and Contracting business systems, to executing procurement data standard (PDS) compliance reviews, contract writing, metrics; troubleshooting and providing strategic communications to and on behalf of the contracting workforce regarding E-Business tools reminders, compliance status, best practices and training material. Provide support to E-Business data analysis, system metrics, reporting process development, and administration of information technology projects and programs in support of Agency procurement and acquisition initiatives. Represent MDA Contracting in internal and external meetings, audits, internal reviews and communications, independently determining appropriate actions to be taken and speaking for the organization. Presenting briefings to senior officials within the agency and other internal and external agency partners. Ensure all actions and tasking are tracked, fully vetted, properly staffed, meet all reporting requirements, and completed in advance of deadlines to ensure time for thorough review and submittal. Identifies concepts, organizational impacts and directs the development and issue of standardized processes and instructions to improve efficiency and effectiveness of the office and operations. Develop recommendations on critical trade-off s regarding courses of action, cost and schedule, identifying associated risks and determining resources required. Serve as MDA's Change Management Agent for business process changes in support of DOD E-Business regulatory, standards and general best practices. Support knowledge management and implement relevant training to workforce to ensure proper system(s) usage and compliance.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: At the Defense Health Agency (DHA), our Mission is to support the National Defense Strategy and Service Military Departments by leading the Military Health System (MHS) as an integrated, highly reliable system of medical training, readiness, and health. As the health care delivery arm of the MHS, DHA is crucial to supporting the Department of Defense's integrated system of readiness and health. DHA manages a global health care network of military and civilian medical professionals and more than 400 military hospitals and clinics around the world. DHA is a joint, integrated Combat Support Agency that enables the Army, Navy, and Air Force medical services to provide a medically ready force and ready medical force to Combatant Commands in both peacetime and wartime. The DHA supports the delivery of integrated, affordable, and high quality health services to the MHS beneficiaries and is responsible for driving greater integration of clinical and business processes across the MHS.

DRUG-FREE WORKPLACE: The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) has established a Drug-Free Federal Workplace Policy. All applicants tentatively selected for DLA employment in a testing designated position are subject to urinalysis to screen for illegal drug use prior to appointment. Applicants who refuse to be tested will be denied employment with DLA for a period of six months. This policy extends to random testing for the use of illegal drugs by employees who occupy testing designated positions defined as sensitive in Section 7(d) of Executive Order 12564. The Defense Logistics Agency's Drug Free Workplace Plan's drug testing panel includes testing for the following illegal substances: marijuana, cocaine, opiates (codeine/morphine), 6-Acetylmorphine (heroin), phencyclidine, amphetamines (amphetamine/methamphetamine), methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA), methylenedioxyamphetamine (MDA), oxycodone, oxymorphone, hydrocodone, and hydromorphone. ADVISORY: By using cannabidiol (CBD) products you are risking a positive drug test result for marijuana.

Details.JobSummary: THIS IS A NATIONAL GUARD TITLE 32 EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITION. This National Guard position is for a Program Analyst, Position Description Number D1010000 and is part of the ND RRO, National Guard.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: THIS IS A NATIONAL GUARD TITLE 32 EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITION. The National Guard is the oldest component of the Armed Forces of the United States. Since the earliest American colonial days, citizens have joined together for collective defense. We have a proud tradition of coming to the aid of our friends and neighbors in times of serious emergencies. Join our National Guard team and serve your nation, your states and your community! The Roughrider Chapter 112 of The Association of Civilian Technicians recognizes the rights afforded to employees under the Federal Service Labor Management Relations Statute to bargain collectively, organize and to participate in any labor organization of their choosing.
MajorDuties: As a Program Analyst, you will serve as the analyst and consultant for the management and administration of programs within the directorate or division. Provides expert technical guidance and specialized team leadership to civilian and military employees. Plans, organizes, performs technical analyses as required, and as assigned, manages budget functions to support programs essential to North Dakota Army National Guard daily readiness missions. Utilizes particular areas of expertise to foster technical excellence in an environment conducive to teaming among service providers and customers to meet North Dakota Army National Guard requirements. Reviews, evaluates, and analyzes obligations and expenditures. Based on budget guidance received from higher headquarters, develops an annual budget for programs. Develops, collects, and maintains various historical data used to initiate planning, programming and execution of current and future training and operations programs.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-09 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: (1) Overseeing for the overall PA and inspection surveillance program, government estimates, documentation and the enforcement of safety standards on facilities maintenance, repair and service contracts; (2) Serving as primary point of contact for the PWD management staff; the Community Manager; Contracting Officer; and the Manager, FSC Branch on matters relating to the Contractor's performance, assessment of services, the Government's preparation of specifications, gathering information for Data Calls as requested by the FMFS Branch Head, and other duties as directed; (3) Maintaining the collection point for the BMS processes keeping the PARs and FMFS Branch Head updated on any changes/updates as they occur; (4) Maintaining Post-award duties which include: pre-work meetings; development of Performance Assessment Plans (PAPs) and Functional Assessment Plans (FAPs); inspections and documenting Contractor Performance; (5) Determining the appropriate method of documentation; (6) Reviewing Contractor's submittals, reports and work schedules; (7) Developing inspection schedules; enforcing safety provisions; validating and preparing contract modification packages; calculating deductions and liquidating damages; certifying invoices and payments; providing customer assistance; providing assistance in negotiation of contract modifications in work orders; preparation of Performance Statements of Work for subsequent contracts; and work authorization. The contract may include custodial, grounds, air-conditioning maintenance, construction, environmental, fire protection maintenance and various others as required; (8) Preparing contract documents (drawings, specifications, costs estimates, Task Orders, BPA Calls, Contract Modifications, Task Order Modifications and BPA Call Modifications for FSC contracts and service indefinite delivery contracts; (9) Preparing Contract Modifications for Firm Fixed Price Contracts; (10) Preparing Indefinite Quantity Work Statements for the government service provider; (11) Preparing detailed material and labor cost estimates using estimating handbooks software and/or engineering performance standards for FSC service contracts, contract modifications and government service provider work and (12) Visiting work sites to collect date pertaining to the scope of work, determines the amount and type of labor and material required Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management web site: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a SENIOR PERFORMANCE ASSESSMENT REPRESENTATIVE in the Naval Facilities Engineering Command, Mid-Atlantic, Facilities Engineering and Acquisition Division, FSC Branch of NAVFAC ENGINEERING CMD MID-ATLANTIC.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will use automated systems for management reports and presentations.
You will use Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting Systems (CPARS) to compose reports on contractor performance.
You will advise management on various types of contract strategies related to business operations to achieve optimum results.
You will monitor contractor performance (e.g., ability to deliver products, services, and systems to contract schedule and within cost) to ensure quality of work.
You will identify areas requiring improvement and effect needed changes in work distribution, utilization of resources, facilities or services, and automated system.
You will identify problems in contractor performance to make recommendations for solutions.

SF-50s that have an effective date within the past year (e.g., General Adjustment SF-50 from this year or Within Rate/Grade Increases (WRI/WGI) SF-50 within a year) do not clearly show that you meet the one-year time-in-grade requirement. If you were issued a DD-215 to amend aforementioned information on the DD-214 you must submit that too. If you are not sure of your preference eligibility, visit the Department of Labor's website: Veterans' Preference Advisor Are you a disabled veteran or claiming 10-point veterans' preference? Policy information may be found at: http://www.secnav.navy.mil/donhr/Documents/CivilianJobs/FedCivAnnuitants.pdf ICTAP Applicants: To be considered well-qualified and exercise selection priority as an ICTAP candidate, displaced Federal employees must satisfy all qualification requirements for the position and receive a rating in the highly qualified category (score 85) or higher. This position is subject to work an uncommon tour, including nights, weekends, and holidays to meet mission requirements. Overtime or night differential pay and/or unusual duty hours may be required. This position is eligible for part time, substantial or ad-hoc telework at the discretion of management. Physical Demands: The work requires extended periods of walking, kneeling, crouching, stooping, and climbing ladders while inspecting buildings, equipment, and grounds. Incumbent visits construction and production sites on a regular and recurring basis. Driving is required for site and customer visits. Work Environment: Work is performed both indoors and outdoors. Incumbent is exposed to temperature extremes, dust, dirt, poor ventilation, and dampness when inspecting grounds, exposed areas, piers, and void spaces under buildings. Work is performed at construction sites.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-09 grade level in the Federal service which includes 1) develop and execute assignments and tasks which consist of laws, regulations, directives, and policies that effect current operations, training, ammunition, and operation orders within the organization; 2) provide expertise and guidance to activities in the areas of contingency missions and current operations; AND 3) act independently, within the guidelines to develop and execute assignments and tasks. OR Education: Ph.D or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the second year (total graduate semester hours minus 36) by 18. Add the two percentages. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.

Abide by security measures when coordinating plan development with higher headquarters.

Details.JobSummary: THIS IS A NATIONAL GUARD TITLE 32 EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITION. This National Guard position is for a FAMILY PROGRAM SPECIALIST (TITLE 32), Position Description Number NGD1743000 and is part of the TN ARMY National Guard.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: THIS IS A NATIONAL GUARD TITLE 32 EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITION. The National Guard is the oldest component of the Armed Forces of the United States. Since the earliest American colonial days, citizens have joined together for collective defense. We have a proud tradition of coming to the aid of our friends and neighbors in times of serious emergencies. Join our National Guard team and serve your nation, your states and your community! This position is located in the Joint Force Headquarters (State), Manpower and Personnel Directorate (J-1), Support Programs Division. The primary purpose of this position is to serve as a team member and advisor on Family Program issues, assist in the development, planning, implementing, and administering the Family Program concerning family and quality of life issues.
MajorDuties: As a FAMILY PROGRAM SPECIALIST, GS-0301-09, you will serve as an advisor on quality of life and Family Program matters for National Guard and Reserve members with the goal of maximizing retention and readiness. Assist in planning, maintaining, and updating an ongoing system of information and referral for use by the military community. Coordinate dissemination of information. Prepare and disseminate information to staff and units to provide to family members and stimulate interest and support on benefits and entitlements. Receive and maintain volunteer hours contributed; support Family Readiness Groups; design and conduct training programs for volunteers; and design and conduct volunteer recognition activities. Identify key volunteers at the unit level to serve as volunteer coordinators. Serve as representative at conferences and meetings on quality of life and Family Program matters. As required, prepare, explain, and defend budgets relative to quality of life and Family Programs. Plan and coordinate mobilization processes for pre-deployment, deployment, and post-deployment issues. Advise chain of command of current and proposed programs and policies requiring modification to improve family readiness and wellness. Coordinate the state family youth program that addresses issues and concerns of youth related to Guard life and youth readiness and well-being. Perform other duties as assigned.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: You will function as a Management and Program Analyst, GS-0343-12, with the U.S.Army Corps of Engineers, Nashville Division, Operations Division, located in Nashville, TN.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Looking for a great place to work? The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) is one of the best! In 2020, USACE ranked #2 of government large-agency subcomponent! USACE is one of the world's premier public engineering, design, and construction management agencies. We serve the American people, striving to provide the most effective engineering and environmental science solutions to the nation's complex problems affecting national security, the economy and the environment in which we live. USACE offers a team-inspiring and collaborative work environment; providing challenging and rewarding careers across a variety of disciplines. We rely on leaders with vision, creativity, and programmatic and technical expertise to lead us into the future. Align your talents with your passion and find out why the U. S. Army Corps of Engineers is a great place to work! The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Develop miscellaneous operational practices.
Consult with managers and technical staff, develops technical input for management policies and procedures.

Provide oversight and coordination for Division Chief, Branch Chiefs, Operations Managers (OMs) and Business Line Managers (BLMs) for succession planning, training, and comprehensive career development.

Provide managerial and administrative assistance to all levels of management including Division Chief, Branch Chiefs, OMs and BLMs in the form of organizational management, recruitment/outreach, troubleshooting hiring issues.

Make evaluative analysis of administrative aspects of new or established programs, including work measurement and operations, workforce estimations, paperwork and procedures, and resource estimates and utilization.
Coordinate with, or leads teams involved in quality and improvement initiatives.
Facilitate and develop process changes that result in positive improvements in cost, time, and administrative burden without unacceptable reductions in mission and overall program effectiveness.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a INTEGRATED PROGRAM PRODUCT TEAM LEAD (IPT) AND PROGRAM MANAGER/ANALYST of CTR FOR AVIATION TECHNL TRNG.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will advise activities, agencies and customers to improve effectiveness, resource efficiency and resources savings for the organization.
You will develop, monitor and coordinate Integrated Logistics Support (ILS) plans.
You will establish processes tools, business rules, and measures to supportability of these systems across the weapons systems life cycle and the entire training continuum.
You will define aviation training equipment/life cycle support requirements to support the introduction of new or upgraded aircraft weapons systems and components to the Fleet.
You will conduct program studies and analyses to identify ILS requirements, e.g., manpower, materials, facilities, trainers, training devices and services.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-11 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: 1) Recommending changes in manpower distribution to minimize adverse impact from manpower shortages or skill imbalance; 2) Developing solutions to manpower issues; 3) Monitoring classification products to ensure timeliness, accuracy, and quality in accordance with position management principles; 4) Executing civilian personnel programs at the command level; and 5) Processing a variety of request for personnel actions. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management web site: http://www.opm.gov/qualifications/Standards/group-stds/gs-admin.asp and https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/0300/management-and-program-analysis-series-0343/ Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a MANAGEMENT ANALYST in the MANPOWER AND PERSONNEL DEPARTMENT of NETPDC.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will initiate and perform analyses, studies and surveys of organizational alignments, mission assignments and manpower allocations for improving organizational effectiveness and efficiency.

You will perform management analysis surveys and studies of assigned organizations with primary interest on the staffing levels and utilization of personnel, functional relationships and workload factors.
You will provide full management advisory services to management on all phases of personnel management.
You will evaluate guidance applicable to manpower and other required resources in relation to priorities, workload levels, staffing trends and funding projections.
You will conduct position management and reorganization studies, review vacant and encumbered positions, processes a variety of requests for personnel action, and participates in efficiency reviews.
You will provide civilian personnel management coordination services.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: GS-07: Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the next lower grade level (GS-05) or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: 1) Identifying, analyzing and recommending solutions to problems in organizational structures, staffing, and administrative procedures; 2) Performing Government Credit Card Requester/Reviewer duties and responsibilities; 3) Utilizing interrelationships of the production line and the support groups at an aircraft maintenance activity; and 4) Preparing briefings using Microsoft office software (Power Point, Excel, Word). GS-05: Your resume must demonstrate at least three years of general experience that includes one year of experience equivalent to the next lower grade level (GS-04) or pay band in the federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. General experience demonstrates the following: Analyze problems to identify significant factors, gather pertinent data, and recognize solutions; Plan and organize work; and Communicate effectively orally and in writing. Examples may include the following: 1) Helping analyze problems in organizational structures, staffing, and administrative procedures; 2) Assisting with Government Credit Card Requester/Reviewer duties and responsibilities; 3) Basic knowledge of interrelationships of the production line and the support groups at an aircraft maintenance activity; and 4) Utilizing Microsoft office software to assist in preparing briefings. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management web site: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

MajorDuties: You will prepare narrative reports, charts and graphs as needed to assist the manager to ensure appropriate personnel actions are generated to prevent such things as incorrect assignments, lost pay and merit system principles violations.

You will work closely with other Management and Program Analysts to support the Production Line and Support Divisions in the efficient and effective functioning of the group, and develop and implement related policies, processes and procedures.

You will receive purchase requests from customers including mass-material purchases, research appropriate items and/or materials, and verify that items and/or materials are not available from mandatory sources.

You will create multi-team and complex travel arrangements, both in country and internationally, utilizing the Defense Travel System and coordinating travel information with the traveler and the travel office/TMC.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.OrganizationName: Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff
MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You may qualify at the GS-14, if you fulfill the following qualifications: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 grade level in the Federal service: Engages in planning and deployment execution for conventional forces to determine appropriate force application (size/mix, Active and/or Reserve Components) to meet supported geographic combatant command capability requirements and ensuring forces are employed based on approved operations and authorities. Formulates and coordinates the execution of providing sourcing continuity regarding the development, formulation and implementation of sourcing solutions related to Joint Individual Augmentee (IA) requirements. Manages complex, joint individual augmentation sourcing activities and coordinates the submissions of all personnel involved in providing operational Joint Task Force (JTF) sourcing inputs for the current Fiscal Year (FY) Global Force Management Allocation Plan (GFMAP). Applies a broad range of personnel augmentation requirements, functions, mission objectives, sponsors, management and functional interfaces, and complex strategic planning to support combatant command contingency operations. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The incumbent will be responsible for providing trained and ready forces in support of global requirements, reporting directly to the Secretary of Defense through the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Mission Statement: The J-3 (Operations), supports the Chairman in carrying out responsibilities as the principal military advisor to the President and Secretary of Defense, developing and providing guidance to the combatant commanders and relaying communications between the President and the Secretary of Defense and the combatant commanders regarding current operations and plans.
MajorDuties: As a SUPERVISORY FORCE ANALYST at the GS-0301-14 some of your typical work assignments may include: Responsible for the supervision of all personnel assigned to the Branch (1-O5; 3-GS-13s, 1-GS12 AND 1-GS-11) and coordinates initial and successive training for all personnel, both active and reserve components on Global Force Management (GFM), Joint Force Coordinator (JFC) and IA programs and processes Directs the development, review; analysis and represents the Joint Staff on all matters that involve sourcing solutions for Joint Individual Augmentees (IA) assigned in support of Joint Manning Documents (JMDs). Formulates and coordinates the execution of providing sourcing continuity and expertise regarding the development, formulation and implementation of sourcing solutions related to Joint Individual Augmentee (IA) requirements. Serves as a subject matter expert in the field of Individual Augmentation, command relationships, Title Ten authorities, strategic planning, and all associated DoD policies, regulations and practices to serve as principal advocate consultant and manager advisor. Oversees management of the Joint Staff Action Process-Next (JSAP-Next) taskers assigned to the IA Branch ensuring appropriate distribution of the workload among the workforce.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a Management Analyst at the COMHELSEACOMBATWING LANT.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will review staff squadron manpower resources.

You will conduct comprehensive analysis and revaluation of tasking, mission requirements, organization, workload, and manpower resources to improve effectiveness, resource efficiency, and ensure successful mission accomplishment.
You will evaluate critical readiness indicators.

You will be the liaison with the Bureau of naval Personnel (BUPERS), Manning Control Authority BUPERS (MCAB PERS-453), Commander Naval air Forces Atlantic Fleet, and Commander Naval air Forces (CNAF).
You will prepare and present briefs, factual reports, charts, and other documentation and defends presentation against impacts to organization objectives and mission accomplishment.

You will utilize the readiness Information system (RIS) to obtain/download data for the purpose of tracking, clarifying analyzing, evaluating and preparing studies, reports, and impact statements concerning personnel manning and readiness.
You will interact with all levels of management in discussing critical and controversial manpower observations, findings, and recommendations.
You will attend meetings, conduct briefings and training sessions on manpower and personal requirements, utilization, distribution, tasking, mission requirements and organization.
You will evaluate requests for manpower changes recommended by staff and subordinate units.
You will coordinate manpower surveys conducted periodically by teams from higher command.
You will provide basic data for use by Fleet/shore Manpower Requirement Determination (FMRD/SMRD) survey teams.
You will prepare concurrence and/or reclaims to manpower survey findings.

Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: Experience applying knowledge of the Surface Force to include Surface Warface Enterprise (SWE) charter, mission and goals. Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a PROGRAM ANALYST in the WARFIGHTING REQUIREMENTS AND ASSESSMENT (N8) DIVISION of COMNAVSURFLANT.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will assist with the Surface Force Commander in the planning, coordination, programming, and assessments of all surface force warfare requirements, and effective warfare improvement programs.
You will serve as an analyst, subject matter and technical expert in analyzing the Surface warfare program requirements.
You will provide expertise in relation to Surface Warfare Ordnance and Unmanned Systems (UXS) requirements.
You will analyze and track changes to the current status of ship ordnance and Optimized Fleet Response Plan (OFRP) schedules for budget formulation.
You will act as the Subject Matter Expert (SME) for Non-Nuclear Ordnance Requirements (NNOR).
You will monitor, evaluate, analyze and advise on prevailing Navy policy and programing decisions affecting Surface Warfare requirements and assessment program.
You will participate in the implementation of requirements supporting Surface Force warfighting capabilities short and long-term (5+ years) budget.
You will advocate new and innovative warfare requirement programs for potential force wide implementation.
You will conduct various cost/benefit program and organizational analysis for Warfighting Requirements and Assessments.
You will prepare periodic financial progress and status reports.
You will identify and propose solutions to systemic limitations and risks to requirements supporting Surface Force warfighting capabilities.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. MajorDuties: You will provide program support to program managers and functional directors for new and existing business.
You will advise the Director on all long-range strategic initiatives that will affect the future direction of the Military Sealift Command (MSC).
You will perform detailed program assessment in support of MSC maritime transformation initiatives for Navy, other Services, DOD, USTRANSCOM, and the Maritime Administration (MARAD).
You will provide innovative solutions to support maritime missions and obtain best value results for Naval operating forces worldwide as well as other DOD and Government agencies.
You will develop, track, and analyze key performance indicators, at both the strategic and operational level, that can be used to evaluate overall performance and influence decision making.

You will plan, organize, and execute command leadership symposiums, industry outreach events, and routine drumbeat events with applicable Fleet Commanders to facilitate and achieve war fighting objectives.
You will manage command coordination and input to the USFFC Baseline Configuration Change Plan (BCCP), System Wholeness Assessment (SWA), and Capability/Capacity (C/CA) Analysis.

You will act as the command manager of the Aquisition Management Systems (AMS), including the Procurement Mangement Tool (PMT), Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) Tool, and Common Spend Plan Tool (CSPT).
You will manage the command task management system to include receipt, assignment, tracking and completion of all command internal and external tasks.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a PROGRAM MANAGER in the NAVFAC HQ, BRAC PROGRAM MANAGEMENT OFFICE of BASE REALIGNMENT AND CLOSURE PMO.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will compose program plans for organizational direction and guidance (e.g., planning, training, funds, schedules, requirements).
You will negotiate differing courses of action between project or program stakeholders to resolve incompatibilities.
You will collaborate with personnel (e.g., key action officers, integrated product team leads) to meet program requirements.
You will brief decision makers on the progress towards meeting program objectives.
You will address program problems and issues by applying the techniques of process identification and continuous process improvement.
You will develop briefings for the delivery of program information to government leaders and key groups.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: GS-07 Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-05 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector performing the following duties: 1) Analyzes existing and projected resources to identify problems and solutions; 2) Maintains program data records to substantiate recommendations; and 3) Assists management with compiling/analyzing statistical and other various types of data, while ensuring the accuracy of information collected; and 4) Ensures the supervisor is briefed on any issues regarding reports and correspondence. and 5) Applies budget and accounting principles on various reports. GS-09 Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-07 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector performing the following duties: 1) Applies analytical and evaluative methods to determine discrepancies, variances, omissions and/or conflicting financial data in various reports; and 2) Provides advice and support on program funding and related policies, procedures, and requirements; 3) Utilizes various computer programs including databases and spreadsheets (E.g. Microsoft Office products, Defense Travel System (DTS), COGNOS) to assist in entering, correcting, and retrieving financial data; 4) Reviews and approves travel orders in Defense Travel System (DTS); and 5) Provides support to the Senior Program Analysts as needed. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management web site: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a PROGRAM ANALYST in the Budget and Resource Management, Capital Improvements (CI) Business Line, Business office of NAVAL FACILITIES ENG COMMAND ATLANTIC in Norfolk, VA
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will monitor program operations to determine the need for reallocation of resources.
You will analyze financial or budget information to determine program effectiveness.
You will develop spreadsheets to track, analyze, and report status of funds.
You will collect, compile, or organize data for review by others.
You will present reports on issues (e.g., budget, problem resolution, management planning, policy issues) to managers.
You will prepare written reports from analysis of financial databases.
You will serve as the Primary Point of Contact in the timely review and certification of travel requests using the Defense Travel System.
You will process incoming reimbursable funding documents and miscellaneous documents through the funds workflow process using eTracker, CFMS and Maximo database.
You will analyze funding status to insure sufficient project funds are available and take appropriate steps to get funds assigned as needed.
You will assist in coordinating briefings involving preparing texts, graphs, charts to effectively express information in written and oral presentations.
You will develop various automated reports for use in analyzing trends affecting project execution and monitoring funding.
Details.Education: If using education in lieu of specialized experience: GS-07: You may qualify with the following substitution of education: 1) One full year of graduate level education; OR 2) Have successfully completed a Bachelor's degree with Superior Academic Achievement; OR 3) Have a combination of experience and education as described above that equates to one year of experience. GS-09: Master's or equivalent graduate degree OR 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree OR LL.B. or J.D., if related A transcript must be submitted with your application if qualifying using education. See Required Documents for additional information.

Generally, only best qualified candidates will be referred to the hiring manager. Sometimes well qualified and minimally qualified candidates are referred. Occasionally, candidates eligible for priority consideration are referred, and no other candidates are referred. The hiring manager may choose to conduct interviews. You will be notified of our rating and referral decision. If you are referred, you will be notified when a hiring decision is made. NOTE: Due to COVID19, if you have any questions or need assistance, please email the DON Employment Information Center at DONEIC@us.navy.mil
Details.RequiredDocuments: You are required to provide documentation that supports the eligibility and qualification claims made in your resume and assessment questionnaire. You must submit the applicable documents listed here and those listed with the eligibilities you select in the announcement questionnaire with your application package. Applicants who do not provide supporting documentation that fully support their claims will not be referred to the hiring manager. Cover letter is optional. A complete resume is required. Your resume must show relevant experience, job title, duties and accomplishments. Your resume must show complete information for each job entry to support minimum qualifications. The following information should be provided in your resume, but it is acceptable to provide elsewhere in your application package: employer's name, starting and end dates (Mo/Yr), hours per week, and pay plan, series and grade level (e.g. GS-0201-09) for relevant federal experience.TIP: A good way to ensure you include all essential information is to use the Resume Builder in USAJOBS to create your resume. Are you claiming membership in any professional organizations, or possession of a license, certificate or credentials? Check the Conditions of Employment section above to see if any are required. If you claim membership, license, certification, or credentials, you must submit a copy of said document in your application package. Are you using education as a substitute for some or all of the experience requirement? Is there a basic education requirement for this position? Check the Education section above to see what is allowed and what is required. Any claims you make in your resume or assessment questionnaire regarding education or degrees MUST be supported by submitting with your application official or unofficial transcripts or a list of courses, grades earned, completion dates, and quarter and semester hours earned issued from your school. While unofficial transcripts are acceptable for initial application, an official transcript will ultimately be required if you are selected for the position. You may submit a copy your degree(s) if specific coursework does not have to be verified. Are you a veteran claiming 5-point veterans' preference or claiming sole survivorship preference? You must submit a copy of your latest DD-214 Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty (any copy that shows all dates of service, as well as character of service [Honorable, General, etc.] is acceptable) OR a VA letter that shows dates of service or service connected disability AND character of service. If you have more than one DD-214 for multiple periods of active duty service, submit a copy for each period of service. If you were issued a DD-215 to amend aforementioned information on the DD-214 you must submit that too. If you are not sure of your preference eligibility, visit the Department of Labor's website: Veterans' Preference Advisor Are you a disabled veteran or claiming 10-point veterans' preference? If you are eligible to claim 10 point veterans preference you must submit a DD-214 Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty as described above for 5-point preference. You must also provide the applicable supporting documentation of your disability (e.g. disability letter from the VA) as described on Standard Form-15 (SF-15). http://www.opm.gov/forms/pdf_fill/SF15.pdf. Are you an active duty service member? Active Duty Service Members are required to submit a statement of service printed on command letterhead and signed by the command. The statement of service must provide the branch of service, rate/rank, all dates of service, the expected date of discharge and anticipated character of service (Honorable, General, etc.). Documents submitted as part of the application package, to include supplemental documents, may be shared beyond the Human Resources Office. Some supplemental documents contain personal information such as SSN and DOB and some documents such as military orders and marriage certificates may contain personal information for someone other than you. You may sanitize these documents to remove said personal information before you submit your application. You must provide an un-sanitized version of the documents if you are selected.

This position is covered by the Department of Defense Priority Placement Program. A 40 hour work week is typical for this position. This position is being recruited at the full performance level. Term appointments may be extended up to 8 years at the discretion of management and in accordance with applicable regulations. Additionally, you may be noncompetitively converted to a permanent career-conditional or career appointment under specific conditions. Certain incentives (such as Recruitment, Relocation or Student Loan Repayment) may be authorized to eligible selectees. A relocation incentive is generally a single payment intended to offset some of the relocation costs experienced by the selectee. A relocation incentive may be authorized. Additional vacancies may be filled by this announcement. A tentative offer of employment will be rescinded if the selectee fails to meet the pre-employment requirements, including failure to report to any of the scheduled appointments. If you are unable to apply online and request information about the Alternate Application process, please contact the Department of Navy's Employment Information Center. Federal annuitant information: The selection of an annuitant is subject to the Department of Defense and Department of the Navy policy on the employment of annuitants. Policy information may be found at: http://www.secnav.navy.mil/donhr/Documents/CivilianJobs/FedCivAnnuitants.pdf ICTAP Applicants: To be considered well-qualified and exercise selection priority as an ICTAP candidate for this vacancy, displaced Federal employees must satisfy all qualification requirements for the position and receive a rating in the highly qualified category or higher. ICTAP candidates must provide copies of all of the following documentation at the time of application: 1) agency notice; 2) most recent performance appraisal and 3) most recent SF-50 or notification of personnel action that includes position, grade level, and duty location. Applicants who do not provide this documentation will not receive consideration as an ICTAP candidate. For more information about ICTAP eligibility please review the following link: https://www.usajobs.gov/Help/working-in-government/unique-hiring-paths/federal-employees/ictap/ Military Spouse Preference applicants will receive priority consideration at the Full Performance Level (FPL) and if determined to be Best Qualified at the FPL, and selected, must be placed at the FPL. A BQ military spouse possesses knowledge, skills, abilities, and competencies comparable to others who meet the competitive referral criteria for the specific position.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a ACADEMIC AFFAIRS ADMINISTRATIVE SPECIALIST in the Academic Affairs Office of NAVAL POSTGRADUATE SCHOOL.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will manage a number of programs and initiatives in support of an academic enterprise.
You will advise managers or personnel on matters pertaining to contracting, accounting, budgeting, or project management.
You will be responsible for oversight, planning, management and execution of resources in support of an academic program.
You will be responsible for administering business processes and coordination activities of the Academic Affairs Office.
Details.Education: In lieu of specialized experience, you may qualify with the following education or combination of both education and experience: master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.B. or J.D., if related A transcript must be submitted with your application if qualifying using education. See Required Documents for additional information.

Therefore, we encourage you to be clear and specific when describing your experience. When the application process is complete, we will review your resume to ensure you meet the hiring eligibility and qualification requirements listed in this announcement. You will be rated based on the information provided in your resume and responses to the Occupational Questionnaire, along with your supporting documentation to determine your ability to demonstrate the following competencies: BUSINESS OPERATIONS COMPUTER LITERACY WRITTEN COMMUNICATION You should list any relevant performance appraisals and incentive awards in your resume as that information may be taken into consideration during the selection process. If selected, you may be required to provide supporting documentation. If after reviewing your resume and supporting documentation, a determination is made that you inflated your qualifications and/or experience, your score may be adjusted to more accurately reflect your abilities or you may be found ineligible/not qualified. Please follow all instructions carefully. Errors or omissions may affect your rating or consideration for employment. All eligibility, qualifications, and time-in-grade requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-05 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: GS-07: Experience with military personnel program/functions and principles. Perform as the SME in military administrative, personnel, training, educational services, family care, military pay, individual augmentation, and travel processes. Experience applying administrative and personnel laws, policies, regulations, and precedents applicable to the administration of military personnel assigned to NNSY and its sub-components. Experience utilizing NNSY Program Goals and Objectives and its relationship with other programs and key administrative and personnel support functions within the Navy. Experience maintaining and exhibiting expert knowledge of the theory and principles of management, organizational design, personnel and administration. Experience with practical qualitative and quantitative analytical techniques to include work measurement, task analysis, job structuring, productivity charting, flow charting or work processes. Experience applying skill and ingenuity in designing and conducting comprehensive management studies, and preparing solutions to especially broad, critical and extensive management problems. Experience delivering products per Navy and internal guidelines and policies. Experience applying grammar, punctuation and spelling are used accurately. Experience handling Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and Health Insurance Portability Accountability Act laws and regulations. Experience conducting research using Master Military Pay Account (MMPA) system online to resolve pay discrepancies. Experience arranging Non-DTS Entry Agent (NDEA) and working directly with military travelers, preparing Travel Orders in Defense Travel System (DTS) and assisting travelers with Travel Claim liquidation within required time requirements. Experience acting as a primary customer service point of contact for all military personnel assigned to NNSY and its sub-components in providing support for all pay and personnel administrative requirements. Experience applying DoD, DON, SECNAV, OPNAV, NPPSC, NETPDTC and BUMED policies and regulations pertaining to personnel, record, and pay administration for the business practices require analytical interpretation of DoD, DON, SECNAV, OPNAV, NPPSC, NETPDTC, and BUMED policies in order to carry out each facet of the position accurately. Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a MILITARY MANAGEMENT SPECIALIST in the Military Support Division (MSD) (Code 100B1) under the Deputy Shipyard Commander (Code100B) at the Norfolk Naval Shipyard in Portsmouth, VA.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will serve as a subject matter expert responsible for providing authoritative recommendations, decisions, or information when rules and regulations may not be readily available.
You will make detailed regulatory and procedural review of special cases involving a full range of potential issues.
You will make recommendations or in some cases make final determinations on actions to be taken in matters of major career or service significance.
You will provide information to outside agencies when requested.
You will review/evaluate business reports, key trends and process indicators.
You will prepare Travel Orders in the Defense Travel System (DTS) and assist with travel claims.
Details.Education: SUBSTITUTION OF EDUCATION FOR EXPERIENCE: Applicants may substitute the following education for the required experience, provided it demonstrates the knowledge, skills and abilities necessary to do the work of the position: GS-05: Successful completion of a full 4-year course of study in any field leading to a bachelor's degree, in an accredited college or university. GS-07: 1 full year of graduate level education or completed a bachelor's degree with Superior Academic Achievement (S.A.A.). COMBINATION OF EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE: Equivalent combinations of education and experience may be used to meet the total qualification requirements but must equate to a total of one hundred percent. A copy of transcript must be submitted.
